summary:
Rostov Oblast has no regional law of its own on gender identity or expression. The national framework of Russia governs in full, and the national assessment carries the legal position that applies to visitors here.

The region's documented support infrastructure is legal rather than protective. A UK Home Office country policy note issued in June 2025 records LGBT+ legal support clinics operating in the Rostov region.

Survey data for the Southern Federal District, which contains Rostov Oblast, put discrimination from healthcare providers who knew a patient's sexual orientation or gender identity at 27%. The figure is district-wide and cannot be read as an oblast-specific rate.
tangentialFactors: The district-level discrimination figure is the only quantitative measure below national level in the source inventory, and it places healthcare-provider discrimination in the Southern Federal District at 27% across several units that include Rostov Oblast.
localsOnly: Residents who need help on sexual orientation or gender identity matters have documented access to LGBT+ legal support clinics in the Rostov region. The district survey indicates that a substantial share of residents report discrimination from healthcare providers once those providers know their status. No regional body records or investigates such discrimination.
outOfScopeNotes: The inventory holds no Rostov-specific enforcement incidents, prosecutions or violence data. The 27% healthcare discrimination figure is recorded for the Southern Federal District as a whole and cannot be isolated to Rostov Oblast. No regional anti-discrimination or hate-crime provision exists that could be assessed separately from the national framework.
